# beszel_quiet_hours (Resource)

Manages a quiet hours window, during which alert notifications are muted for a user, either for every system or for one system.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Mute notifications for every system, every night from 22:00 to 06:00 UTC.
# For daily windows only the UTC time of day of start and end matters.
resource "beszel_quiet_hours" "nightly" {
  user  = beszel_user.example.id
  type  = "daily"
  start = "2026-01-01T22:00:00Z"
  end   = "2026-01-02T06:00:00Z"
}

# Mute one system during a planned maintenance window.
resource "beszel_quiet_hours" "maintenance" {
  user   = beszel_user.example.id
  system = beszel_system.example.id
  type   = "one-time"
  start  = "2026-06-01T01:00:00Z"
  end    = "2026-06-01T03:00:00Z"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `end` (String) End of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `start` (String) Start of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `type` (String) Kind of window. `one-time` mutes notifications from `start` (inclusive) until `end` (exclusive), so `end` must be after `start`. `daily` repeats every day: only the UTC time of day of `start` and `end` matters, the two must differ, and the window may cross midnight (for example 22:00 to 06:00).
- `user` (String) ID of the user whose notifications are muted.

### Optional

- `system` (String) ID of the system the window applies to. Omit to apply it to all systems.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) PocketBase record ID of the quiet hours window.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By PocketBase record id (Beszel has no natural key for quiet hours windows,
# so the record id is the only way to import one):
terraform import beszel_quiet_hours.nightly i4bzj802ik
```
